system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: HOPE-3 NCT00468923 - Heart Outcomes Prevention Evaluation-3
Investigational drug: rosuvastatin
Document: Population pharmacokinetics of rosuvastatin in pediatric patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (journal, published 2015-09-21, source pmid:26387811)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Population pharmacokinetics of rosuvastatin in pediatric patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia

PURPOSE: Data from two clinical studies (hyperCholesterolaemia in cHildren and Adolescents taking Rosuvastatin OpeN label [CHARON; NCT01078675] and Study 4522IL/0086) were used to describe rosuvastatin pharmacokinetics in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia aged ≥6 to <18 years. METHODS: Rosuvastatin concentration-time data were analyzed via non-linear mixed-effects modeling (NONMEM), with clearance (CL/F) as the pre-defined key pharmacokinetic parameter of interest. In addition, descriptive comparisons between pediatric patients and adults (healthy and dyslipidemic) were performed. The dataset included 214 pediatric patients, with 2,029 rosuvastatin concentrations. RESULTS: A linear two-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination processes adequately described the combined dataset. Weight and gender were significant covariates for CL/F, with moderate between-patient variability remaining (coefficient of variation (CV) 40 %): CL/F in female children was approximately 30 % lower than in male children, and there was a twofold mean difference in CL/F across the observed weight range. Age was not a significant covariate after accounting for weight and gender differences. However, weight and gender only reduced between-patient variability from 45 (without covariates) to 40 % and are considered unlikely to be clinically relevant. CONCLUSIONS: Rosuvastatin pharmacokinetics appeared generally predictable with respect to dose, and time (study duration) and the exposure (dose-normalized area under the plasma concentration-time curve at steady state (AUCss)) in children and adolescents appeared to be similar or lower than adult patients with dyslipidemia.
--- END ---

Extract the facts.
